facts.text: A bicycle is a small land vehicle powered by a person.
A bicycle has two wheels, one in front and one in back.
A bicycle has a seat for the rider to sit on.
A frame holds the bicycle parts together and gives the bike strength.
The rider's feet push the pedals around in circles.
Pedaling helps turn the back wheel and moves the bike forward.
Many bicycles use a chain to connect the pedals to the back wheel.
Bike tires touch the ground and roll along the path.
The handlebars help the rider steer the bicycle.
Turning the handlebars turns the front wheel.
A balance bike lets a young child push with feet while learning to balance.
A steady rider keeps looking ahead while the bike rolls.
A bike helmet should be worn on every ride.
A helmet should fit correctly and have fastened straps.
Bright clothes help riders be easier for other people to see.
Shoes should grip the pedals; children should not ride barefoot.
Many bicycles have brakes to help the rider slow down or stop.
A rider should stop and check both ways before leaving a driveway, alley, or curb.
Bike riders should stop at stop signs and red traffic lights.
A child can walk a bike across a busy crosswalk with a grown-up.
Some places have bicycle paths where riders can stay away from busy car traffic.
Kids younger than 10 should ride on the sidewalk, according to Nemours KidsHealth guidance.
Bike riders should watch for people walking and give them space.
A rider should be careful near driveways because cars can come in or out.
Only one person should sit on a bike seat at a time.
A bicycle bell or horn can help warn people that a rider is coming by.
